title: Part 1 Practice: Introduction to Soils, Weathering, and Soil Properties

options: A) Pure mineral material with no organic content
B) A dynamic natural body composed of mineral particles, organic matter, water, air, and living organisms
C) Only the top layer of rocks
D) A man-made material for construction
questions.correct_answer: B) A dynamic natural body composed of mineral particles, organic matter, water, air, and living organisms
questions.explanation: Correct: Soil is a complex natural body with both mineral and organic components. A is wrong—soil contains organic matter. C is wrong—soil is more than just rock fragments. D is wrong—soil is natural, not man-made.

questions.text: Which type of weathering involves the physical breakdown of rocks without changing their chemical composition?
questions.explanation: Correct: Mechanical weathering breaks rocks physically. A is wrong—chemical weathering changes composition. B is wrong—biological weathering involves organisms. D is wrong—oxidation is a chemical process.

questions.text: In which Ethiopian region is freeze-thaw weathering most active?
questions.explanation: Correct: Freeze-thaw occurs in high-altitude areas with freezing temperatures. A is wrong—Afar is hot and dry. C is wrong—Ogaden is lowland. D is wrong—Rift Valley is warmer.

questions.text: What chemical process involves the reaction of oxygen with iron-bearing minerals in rocks?
questions.explanation: Correct: Oxidation is the reaction with oxygen. A is wrong—hydrolysis involves water. B is wrong—carbonation involves CO₂. D is wrong—solution involves dissolving in water.

questions.text: The red color of Ethiopian Nitisols is primarily due to which chemical weathering process?
questions.explanation: Correct: Oxidation of iron minerals forms iron oxides (hematite) giving red color. A is wrong—hydrolysis forms clay. C is wrong—carbonation dissolves carbonates. D is wrong—hydration absorbs water.

questions.text: Which soil property measures the soil's ability to retain and exchange nutrients?
questions.explanation: Correct: CEC measures nutrient retention. A is wrong—pH measures acidity. B is wrong—texture measures particle size. D is wrong—bulk density measures soil mass.

questions.text: What is the approximate time required to form one centimeter of topsoil?
questions.explanation: Correct: Soil formation is extremely slow—100-400 years per centimeter. A is wrong—too short. B is wrong—still too short. D is wrong—too long; full soil profile takes millennia but topsoil formation is 100-400 years.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian soil type typically has the highest cation exchange capacity (CEC)?
questions.explanation: Correct: Vertisols have high clay content (>50%) giving high CEC (40-60 cmol/kg). A is wrong—Nitisols have 20-30 cmol/kg. C is wrong—Cambisols have moderate CEC. D is wrong—Solonchaks have low CEC due to salinity.

questions.text: How do lichens contribute to soil formation in Ethiopia's highlands?
options: A) By breaking rocks through physical pressure
B) By secreting acids that dissolve rock minerals
C) By adding organic matter through decomposition
D) By holding soil particles together
questions.correct_answer: B) By secreting acids that dissolve rock minerals
questions.explanation: Correct: Lichens secrete organic acids that chemically weather rocks. A is wrong—roots exert physical pressure. C is wrong—lichen decomposition adds organic matter but their main role is chemical weathering. D is wrong—this is a secondary effect.

questions.text: Which physical property of soil is most affected by the proportion of sand, silt, and clay particles?
questions.explanation: Correct: Texture is defined by sand/silt/clay ratios. A is wrong—color is influenced by mineral content. C is wrong—structure is about particle arrangement. D is wrong—porosity is about pore space, influenced but not defined by texture.
